title: Texas Dominates Backstretch; Kyle Whittingham Hits New Low in College Football Upset
body:
The college football landscape shifted dramatically in Week 10, as Texas surged back into relevance with a dominant win that thrust the Longhorns into the national conversation, while Michigan’s first‑year head coach, J.J. McCarthy, endured another setback that underscored the challenges of rebuilding a storied program. The weekend’s marquee matchups also saw No. 1 Miami tumble to No. 11 Notre Dame, extending a streak of upsets that has now claimed five of the top‑two teams in as many weeks, reshaping the College Football Playoff picture and setting the stage for a chaotic run‑in to the postseason.

Texas’ resurgence was anchored by a balanced offensive attack that exploited a vulnerable Oklahoma State defense on both sides of the ball. Quarterback Quinn Ewers, who entered the game with a modest résumé, delivered a poised performance, completing 21 of 28 passes for 312 yards and three touchdowns. His poise in the pocket, combined with a decisive scramble for a fourth score, demonstrated a maturation that had been absent earlier in the season. The Longhorns’ ground game, led by sophomore running back Tyree Wilson, added 145 rushing yards and a touchdown, establishing a credible threat that forced Oklahoma State to defend the entire field. Defensively, Texas forced three turnovers, including a pivotal interception returned for a score in the fourth quarter, sealing a 38‑24 victory that propelled the Longhorns back into the top‑25 and sparked talk of a potential conference championship run.

In stark contrast, Michigan’s weekend was defined by a stuttering offensive showing that left fans and analysts questioning the trajectory of J.J. McCarthy’s inaugural campaign. The Wolverines entered the contest as a defensive powerhouse but were stymied by a disciplined Iowa defense that limited the Michigan offense to a paltry 172 total yards. Quarterback J.J. McCarthy, who has been praised for his leadership, struggled to find rhythm, completing just 13 of 27 attempts with a single touchdown and two interceptions. The loss dropped Michigan to a sub‑.500 record and amplified calls for a faster adjustment period as the program attempts to regain its footing after a tumultuous offseason that saw the departure of several key players and a revamp of the coaching staff.

The ripple effects of these outcomes reverberated across the broader College Football Playoff race. Miami’s 31‑28 defeat at the hands of Notre Dame not only halted the Hurricanes’ unbeaten streak but also knocked them out of the top‑two slot for the first time this season. Notre Dame, buoyed by a resilient second‑half surge, climbed to No. 2, positioning themselves as a dark‑horse contender for the playoff. Meanwhile, Texas’ ascent to No. 9 injects fresh intrigue into the Big 12, a conference that has already seen three different teams claim the top spot this year. Analysts note that Texas’ ability to win convincingly on the road could be a decisive factor when the selection committee evaluates strength of schedule and quality wins.

Beyond the immediate standings, the week highlighted a growing trend of volatility at the summit of college football. Five consecutive weeks have witnessed a top‑two team fall, a pattern not seen since the early 2000s. This instability underscores the increasing parity among elite programs, driven by expanded recruiting footprints, the transfer portal’s impact, and the rapid integration of advanced analytics into game planning. Coaches who can adapt quickly—like Texas’ offensive coordinator Zach Kittley, whose up‑tempo scheme caught opponents off guard—are reaping rewards, while those stuck in legacy systems risk being left behind.

Looking ahead, Texas must sustain its momentum against a formidable Texas A&M squad next Saturday, a game that could solidify their claim as a legitimate contender for the Big 12 title and a potential playoff berth. Michigan, on the other hand, faces a critical test against Ohio State, a rivalry that will likely determine whether the Wolverines can salvage a season that has already slipped below expectations. As the regular season winds down, the fluidity of the rankings promises further surprises, and the next few weeks will be decisive in shaping the narrative for both programs and the national championship picture.
